reviewed_by: Claude review of Workbench side-panel reliability
reason: Two Workbench panels misbehaved on ordinary use. PostToolAssistant's polling effect depended on the config object; each tick ended with refresh(), which stored a fresh config object from Core, so the effect re-armed and ran tick again immediately: with Suggest next steps or Take notes enabled the panel issued executions, runs and post-tool-results requests back to back with no 3 s gap (the new unit test measures 17,510 listExecutions calls in three seconds on main, one after the fix). The effect now depends on the primitive fields it gates on and reads the latest config through a ref. NotesPanel's draft-sync effect depended on the selected note's object identity; every list reload (Refresh notes, or a reload after another change) produced a new object for the same note and reset the editor to the saved copy, discarding unsaved edits, and a reload while a new note was being drafted moved the selection to the first note so Delete targeted it. The sync now keys on note id and revision, and a reload keeps the selection untouched while a note is being created. Frontend tests cover both (unsaved body survives Refresh notes; polling issues one request per interval); the files' other cases cover enablement, runtime gating, note create/edit/delete and Ask Nebula. npm run build typechecks and bundles.
exclusions: No Python tests: no backend change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: PostToolAssistant* and NotesPanel* map to the remaining-ui-components areas desktop-interface and mobile-layout, whose mocked journeys open these panels but do not measure the polling cadence or edit a note across a refresh; the unit tests drive both against the rendered components. No screenshot baselines: no rendered change. No real-browser pass was run in this session. No full suites.
